# Session 11: Pipeline Assembly

## 📋 Agenda

You have already run every piece of this pipeline. Today you learn to **name the structure**.

- **15 min** — the pipeline as one diagram, and where you have met each helper
- **45 min** — your group writes `PLAN.md`
- **25 min** — each group states its I/O contract out loud

::: {.callout-note}
Not a re-teach. Nothing here is new code — the point is being able to *describe* the flow, which is exactly what the Q&A on Day 5 will ask you to do.
:::

## 🎯 Learning Objectives

By the end of this session, you will be able to:

- Describe the pipeline as a chain of **inputs and outputs** — what each step consumes and produces.
- Point to where in Days 1–3 you ran each helper, and use the same call form again.
- Write your group's `PLAN.md` and defend its six lines.

# The pipeline

## One diagram

```
pool ──sample──▶ sampled ──annotate──▶ sheet ──adjudicate──▶ gold
                                                              │
                            prompt ─────────────┐             │
                                                ▼             ▼
                                          run_prompt ──▶ predictions
                                                              │
                                                    save_predictions
                                                              │
                                                              ▼
                                                       FROZEN FILE
                                                              │
                                         ┌────────────────────┤
                                         ▼                    ▼
                                    evaluate              show_errors
                                         │                    │
                                         └──────▶ export ◀─────┘
```

## Read it as data shapes

| Arrow | What flows | Shape |
|---|---|---|
| pool → sampled | ~40 items, balanced | `[{id, text, label}]` |
| sampled → sheet | one row per item, **labels blanked** | a Google Sheet |
| sheet → gold | your adjudicated decisions | `[{id, text, label}]` |
| gold + prompt → predictions | one label per item | `["B1", "A2", …]` |
| predictions → frozen file | the same list, **on disk** | `.json` |
| gold + frozen → metrics | P/R/F1, κ, matrix | numbers you report |

. . .

Everything after the frozen file reads **the file**, not the model.

## Where you have already used these {.smaller}

| Step | Helper | You ran it in | Same call? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `load_gold(path)` | Day 2 S5 · Day 3 | ✅ |
| 1 | `sample_pool(pool, n, seed)` | Day 4 — as four inline steps | one call now |
| 2 | `create_annotation_sheet(...)` | Day 2 S5 step A | ✅ |
| 2 | `load_annotation_sheet(...)` | Day 2 S5 step D | ✅ |
| 2 | `annotator_agreement(rows)` | Day 2 S5 step D | ✅ |
| 2 | `disagreements(rows)` | Day 2 S5 step E | ✅ |
| 2 | `to_canonical(rows, labels)` | Day 2 S5 step F | ✅ |
| 3–4 | `run_prompt(PROMPT, gold)` | Day 3, every round | ✅ |
| 3–4 | `evaluate(gold, pred, ordered=True)` | Day 2 S6 · Day 3 | ✅ |
| 5 | `show_errors(gold, pred)` | Day 3 | ✅ |

**Nine of these are the identical call.** That is why 15 minutes is enough.

## The three that are new

```{.python}
load_prompt(path)                  # your prompt is a FILE now, so versions survive
save_predictions(pred, path)       # the freeze from S10, made executable
export_results(track, gold, pred, f1_by_round, out_dir, group=GROUP)
```

. . .

And one that changes shape:

```{.python}
build_fewshot(PROMPT, pool, gold)  # Day 3: you typed the examples by hand
                                   # now: drawn from the pool, avoiding your gold
```

# `PLAN.md`

## The 作戦シート, finally given a file

You have been building this plan since S3 — track, scheme, gold source, prompting strategy. Today it becomes one page in your repo.

**It is not graded.** It is a **gate**: no group calls the model until it is signed.

. . .

Two minutes of writing catches the failures that otherwise cost an hour *after* you have spent quota:

- label set says `Move 1/2/3`, gold file says `1a/1b`, prompt says "move one" → no error, just a confusing F1
- labels ordered but not alphabetical → weighted κ computed over `High < Low < Mid`
- nobody agreed who codes which column → one annotator, no κ

## The six lines

```markdown
# PLAN — <group>, track <track>
Members: …

1. Unit of analysis: (sentence / whole text) — and why
2. Label set: … (exactly the strings in your gold file)
3. Are the labels ORDERED? In what order?
4. Gold: pool file · N_PER_CLASS · SEED · expected total
5. QC: who is CoderA, who is CoderB, who adjudicates
6. Prompt plan: baseline, then the ONE change you predict
   will help — and why
```

::: {.callout-tip}
Question 3 exists to catch the ordinal-κ trap. Question 6 asks you to **predict before you test** — which is the whole method in one line.
:::

## And the table

| # | Step | Consumes | Produces |
|---|------|----------|----------|
| 1 | sample | `POOL_PATH`, `N_PER_CLASS`, `SEED` | `pool`, `sampled`, `LABELS` |
| 2 | QC / adjudicate | `sampled`, `LABELS`, the sheet | `gold` |
| 3 | baseline | `PROMPT`, `gold` | `pred0`, `f1_by_round` |
| 4 | iterate + freeze | `PROMPT`, `pool`, `gold` | `pred_final` (a file) |
| 5 | error analysis | `gold`, `pred_final` | the errors table |
| 6 | export | all of the above | `outputs/…_report.md` |
